aliyas-journal-051.excerpt: A well-prepared sale starts before the photographs. Put the property's condition, documents, asking-price evidence and access arrangements in order so buyers can assess it with confidence.
aliyas-journal-051.introduction:
Walk through your home as though you have never seen it before. A sticking door, an overflowing cupboard or a question about the parking space may seem minor after years of living there. For a visitor, each one is a piece of information about the property and how it has been looked after.

Preparing for a sale means making that information easier to understand. It also means checking that the paperwork and timing support the transaction you hope to complete. This guide concerns an existing home; an off-plan assignment needs its own developer and contractual checks.
takeaways: Resolve maintenance questions before spending heavily on decoration.
Build a property file that distinguishes confirmed facts from documents still needed.
Agree the marketing, access and handover plan before the listing goes live.

sections.heading: Start with a condition walk-through
sections.body:
Give yourself a quiet hour to inspect the home without doing the usual household jobs. Open doors and cupboards, run taps, look at sealant, check lights and note anything that needs a professional assessment. Photograph the issues for your own repair list, rather than trying to remember them while arranging the listing.

Separate an untidy appearance from a defect. A room can be cleaned in an afternoon; recurring damp, electrical problems or a leaking air-conditioning unit call for appropriate investigation. Painting over a stain without understanding its cause can leave both the problem and the eventual buyer's questions unresolved.

Ask contractors to describe the work completed and keep the receipts. If a repair is unfinished, record its status accurately. The aim is to explain the home's condition honestly, including what has been repaired and what still needs attention, without turning an ordinary property into a claim of perfection.

sections.heading: Gather the documents while there is time
sections.body:
Create one folder for ownership information, relevant plans, service-charge records, alteration approvals, warranties and any tenancy documents. The exact sale requirements depend on the emirate, development, ownership arrangement and financing. Ask the people handling the transaction for a current checklist rather than copying another seller's file.

Developer procedures can be quite specific. The [Dubai Properties resale guide](https://dp.ae/pdf/DP_Resale%20Guide_Handed%20Over%202025.pdf) for handed-over properties with title deeds lists its own seller and buyer documentation and a resale NOC process. That is a useful example of why the property's actual developer matters; it is not a universal checklist for every UAE home.

Check names, property identifiers and contact details across the documents. If an owner will be abroad or someone will act on their behalf, have the relevant authority and professional adviser confirm the representation requirements early. An attractive listing cannot resolve missing authority to sign. Keep sensitive copies in a controlled folder and share them only through the appropriate transaction process.

sections.heading: Decide which improvements deserve the money
sections.body:
Start with cleanliness, maintenance and the way the rooms function. Clear a route from the entrance to the main living area. Move surplus furniture if it prevents people from understanding the layout. Make sure doors can open and that useful storage is visible rather than packed beyond use.

Before committing to a larger upgrade, compare its cost and disruption with the evidence supporting your asking price. A new kitchen chosen to your taste may not appeal to the next owner. Obtain an actual quotation and consider whether completing the work would delay the sale or leave the home difficult to view.

The [home-staging guide](/journal/home-staging-uae) develops the presentation side in more detail. Here, the useful distinction is between work that restores the home to a sound, understandable condition and spending intended to impress. Set a preparation budget, assign each task a priority and stop adding improvements simply because the property is about to be photographed.

table.caption: A practical preparation list
rows: Investigate defects and arrange suitable repairs
Clean, reduce clutter and show room functions
table.note: Planning aid, not a statutory checklist or a quotation for preparation work.

sections.heading: Give the broker one accurate version of the property
sections.body:
Prepare a simple fact sheet: the property identifier, documented area, room layout, parking arrangement, included fittings, occupancy status and any restrictions or unresolved questions. Make clear which details are supported by documents and which still need confirmation. Avoid rounding an area upwards or describing a converted space as an approved bedroom without evidence.

In Dubai, [DLD's Form A circular](https://dubailand.gov.ae/media/io2f5x5c/%D8%B1%D8%A8%D8%B7-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%AD-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%B9%D9%82%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%B3%D9%88%D9%8A%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D9%8A.pdf) links the seller-broker electronic marketing contract with the advertisement-permit process. Review the actual appointment and marketing permissions before publication. Other emirates have their own arrangements, so agree the applicable process with a properly authorised professional.

Keep your asking-price discussion separate from the fact sheet. A price is a commercial decision, while the home's dimensions and tenancy status should remain consistent wherever it appears. Our [asking-price guide](/journal/asking-price-dubai-home) explains how to prepare a reasoned pricing discussion.

sections.heading: Plan access around the people who live there
sections.body:
If the property is occupied, work out a viewing routine before enquiries arrive. Agree who confirms appointments, how much notice is practical, where keys are held and which parts of the home require extra care. A tenant's home is not an unattended showroom; tenancy and legal requirements need separate attention.

Consider pets, children, working hours and building access. Remove personal paperwork from view and put valuables away. Give the broker clear instructions about photography, cupboards, balconies and shared facilities so visitors receive consistent guidance without being allowed unrestricted access.

Leave enough time between appointments to reset the home and answer questions. A rushed sequence of visitors can make the process harder for occupants and less useful for buyers. If viewings must be limited, state the available windows clearly rather than accepting appointments that repeatedly have to be cancelled.

sections.heading: Choose a launch date that the property can support
sections.body:
Work backwards from the point at which the home, documents and photographs will all be ready. A listing can attract interest before you are organised, but that creates pressure to explain unfinished repairs, arrange unsuitable visits or produce documents at short notice. A realistic launch date gives the preparation work an end point.

Agree how feedback will be collected and when the listing will be reviewed. Ask for the questions buyers actually raised, not just a report of clicks or compliments. Repeated uncertainty about a layout, tenancy or service cost is information you can address.

Finally, think about what happens after an offer. Your own moving plan, any mortgage settlement and the proposed handover condition should be considered before accepting a timetable. A prepared seller can discuss those matters clearly, which is more useful than promising the fastest possible completion without checking the dependencies.

aliyas-journal-052.excerpt: Build an asking price from relevant evidence, the home's condition and your selling timetable. Learn to separate comparable sales, competing listings and the amount you hope to receive.
aliyas-journal-052.introduction:
Your neighbour's asking price is easy to find. The price at which a genuinely similar home changed hands, on comparable terms, can take more work. That difference matters when you are deciding where to position your own listing.

An asking price has a job to do: bring the property to the attention of suitable buyers while leaving you with a defensible negotiating position. It is not a promise of the eventual sale price. Nor should it be set only by what you paid or what your next home will cost.
takeaways: Use comparable completed transactions and current competing listings for different purposes.
Explain each adjustment for condition, layout, occupancy or location.
Review the price against meaningful buyer feedback and your own net-proceeds requirements.

sections.heading: Define the property you are actually comparing
sections.body:
Start with the building or community, property type, documented area, bedroom arrangement, floor, outlook, parking and occupancy. A similarly sized apartment nearby may compete with yours, but a different layout or building condition can affect how a buyer uses it. Make a comparison sheet before selecting the examples that support your preferred figure.

Use the same area definition throughout. Do not compare a built-up figure for one property with an internal area for another and treat the resulting price per square foot as precise. Note balconies, terraces, plots and other features separately where their treatment differs.

If the home has been altered, distinguish approved changes from informal descriptions in an advertisement. A study used as a bedroom does not automatically become an equivalent additional bedroom. Accurate comparison begins with a consistent description, even when that description is less flattering than the wording in a competing listing.

sections.heading: Separate sold evidence from asking prices
sections.body:
[DLD's real-estate data service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/open-data/real-estate-data/) provides transaction information for Dubai. It is a starting point for locating relevant evidence, not a ready-made valuation of your particular home. This article has not downloaded a transaction sample or calculated a current market price.

Ask your broker to identify the date, property characteristics and transaction type behind each comparable. An old sale, an off-plan transaction or a property with different occupancy terms may need to be treated differently from a recent completed-home resale. Where a detail is unknown, mark the gap rather than filling it with an assumption.

Current advertisements show the alternatives a buyer can consider. They show what sellers are seeking, not necessarily what buyers have agreed to pay. Keep those listings in a separate column, check whether apparently different advertisements describe the same unit and avoid counting duplicates as evidence of additional supply.

sections.heading: Make adjustments explainable
sections.body:
A price adjustment should answer a specific question. What is different about the outlook? Is the kitchen newly fitted or simply photographed well? Does the parking arrangement suit the likely buyer? Is the home available for occupation on the required timetable? These details should be described before anyone attaches a number to them.

Where possible, ask for matched evidence supporting an adjustment. If that evidence is weak, use a range and explain the uncertainty. Adding an arbitrary premium for every attractive feature can quickly produce a price that no comparable transaction supports.

The table below is a discussion framework rather than a valuation formula. Several differences can overlap: floor level, view and noise may describe the same underlying advantage. Avoid charging for that advantage three times. For a broader buyer-side perspective, see the [guide to fairly priced UAE properties](/journal/fairly-priced-properties-uae).

table.caption: Questions behind an asking-price adjustment
table.note: Original comparison framework; it does not assign a market value or fixed adjustment.

sections.heading: Understand when a formal valuation is useful
sections.body:
A broker's marketing recommendation, a lender's assessment and a formal valuation serve different purposes. Ask what question each assessment is intended to answer and what evidence and assumptions it uses. A single headline number is less helpful if the report's date, inspection scope or occupancy assumptions are unclear.

[DLD's property-valuation service](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/property-valuation) covers residential units and villas among other property types and provides a valuation certificate. Check the current service requirements and whether that service is appropriate for your purpose. The existence of a certificate does not oblige a buyer or their lender to accept your asking price.

A formal assessment can be particularly useful when owners disagree, the property is unusual or the evidence is thin. Explain the intended use to the valuer rather than requesting the highest possible number. If a buyer's lender later reaches a different figure, investigate the assumptions and financing implications instead of treating the difference as proof that either party is acting improperly.

sections.heading: Keep the asking price separate from your cash requirement
sections.body:
Calculate the amount you would actually retain after the relevant loan settlement, agreed selling costs and other obligations. Use current written figures for your own transaction. A gross sale price that sounds acceptable may leave less money available for the next purchase than expected.

Your required proceeds are important to your decision, but they do not establish the market value of the property. If the evidence-supported range cannot meet your needs, reconsider the timing, the next purchase or the available funding. Raising the asking price to close a personal funding gap does not make the gap disappear.

Decide in advance which terms you can negotiate alongside price. A workable completion date or a clearly documented inclusion may matter, but its value depends on your circumstances. The [offer-comparison guide](/journal/compare-property-offers-beyond-price) provides a way to assess those terms without losing sight of the money.

sections.heading: Agree a review process before the listing goes live
sections.body:
Set a review date with the broker and decide what evidence you will examine. Useful information includes qualified enquiries, completed viewings, repeated objections and written offers with their conditions. Online attention alone does not tell you whether the price fits the buyers who can complete a purchase.

If viewings are scarce, examine the presentation, accuracy and reach of the advertisement as well as the price. If viewings are frequent but offers do not follow, ask what visitors consistently found unsuitable. Correct factual gaps and access problems before assuming every difficulty is a pricing problem.

When a price change is justified, update every authorised advertisement together. Keep a record of the decision and the evidence behind it. A clear, consistent asking price helps buyers understand the current proposition and gives you a sound basis for the next conversation, whether that leads to an offer or a decision to wait.

aliyas-journal-053.excerpt: Make your home easier to understand at a viewing. Focus on furniture scale, clear routes, useful light and a few well-chosen changes rather than an expensive makeover.
aliyas-journal-053.introduction:
A dining chair that blocks the balcony door tells a visitor something about a room, even if the room itself is generous. A spare bedroom filled with boxes tells them very little. Home staging is the work of making the space's purpose easier to see.

You do not have to remove every sign of living there or buy a houseful of new furniture. Often the useful changes are modest: moving a piece, clearing a surface, replacing a failed bulb and showing how the rooms connect. The test is whether the home becomes clearer, not merely more decorated.
takeaways: Show a believable use for each room without concealing defects.
Prioritise clear circulation and appropriately scaled furniture.
Treat staging as presentation; it is not evidence of a guaranteed price uplift.

sections.heading: Decide what each room should communicate
sections.body:
Write one sentence for the main purpose of each room. The living area might need to show seating for a household without blocking the route to the terrace. A second bedroom might need to demonstrate that a bed, wardrobe and door clearance can coexist. That sentence becomes the brief for moving or removing furniture.

Do not force every space into the same aspirational lifestyle. A modest apartment can be presented as comfortable and practical without pretending to be a large entertaining home. Keep at least one realistic arrangement that allows visitors to judge how their own belongings might fit.

Photograph the room from its entrance after making changes. If the main function is still unclear, remove another distraction rather than adding more accessories. This is especially useful for rooms with several doors or an awkward corner, where the route through the space matters as much as the furniture itself.

sections.heading: Give buyers room to move
sections.body:
Clear the paths people use during a viewing: entrance to living room, living room to balcony, bed to wardrobe and kitchen to dining area. Avoid creating a narrow obstacle course around decorative pieces. A home should be easy to walk through without visitors feeling that they must squeeze past your possessions.

Check how doors, drawers and cupboards open. Moving a chair slightly may reveal usable storage that was hidden before. Conversely, an attractive arrangement that prevents a wardrobe door from opening makes the layout harder to assess. Keep these practical movements in the plan.

Store removed items sensibly. Pushing everything into the nearest cupboard can undermine the impression when a buyer asks to see inside. If extra storage or furniture rental is needed, obtain a quotation and decide whether the expense fits the likely duration of the listing. There is no need to stage every room to the same degree.

sections.heading: Use the research without promising a result
sections.body:
In the US National Association of REALTORS' [2025 staging survey](https://www.nar.realtor/research-and-statistics/research-reports/profile-of-home-staging), 83% of buyers' agents said staging helped buyers picture a property as a future home. That is a reported opinion from a US professional survey, not a measured UAE sale-price increase or a guarantee that staging will sell your home faster.

Its useful lesson is about understanding space. A visitor should be able to recognise a bedroom, see where everyday items go and judge whether the layout supports their routine. Those are practical presentation goals that you can assess directly, without borrowing an overseas percentage to predict your own sale.

Keep the budget tied to the property. Cleaning and rearranging existing furniture may be enough. If a stager proposes a larger package, ask which specific problem each item solves, what is included in the quotation and how long the furniture or styling will remain available. Make the decision on scope and usefulness, not a promised return.

sections.heading: Work with light, finishes and what is already there
sections.body:
Clean glazing where it can be reached safely and open curtains enough to show the actual outlook. Check that lamps work and that the room's lighting feels consistent. Photograph the home at the time agreed with the photographer, but also consider how it will appear during normal viewing hours.

Use a small number of objects to show scale and function. A table setting can identify a dining area; a desk and chair can explain a working corner. Too many cushions, scented products or decorative arrangements can distract from the room and make it harder for visitors to assess it comfortably.

Deal with the cause of an issue before improving its appearance. A rug should not be used to conceal damaged flooring, and a fragrance should not replace investigating an unexplained smell. The [sale-preparation guide](/journal/prepare-uae-property-for-sale) helps separate maintenance work from presentation tasks.

table.caption: Small staging changes with a clear purpose
rows: Clear the route and show useful storage
Arrange seating around a believable use
Use suitable seating within the available space
Concealing the outlook or unsafe arrangements
table.note: Original presentation checklist, not a promise of higher offers.

sections.heading: Keep the photographs and the viewing consistent
sections.body:
If hired furniture will be removed before viewings, discuss that in advance and describe the change accurately. The same applies to digitally furnished images: distinguish the proposed arrangement from what is physically present. A buyer should not have to guess whether the kitchen, view or furniture they saw online exists in the home.

Staging does not replace the marketing process. In Dubai, [DLD's advertisement-permit service](https://backoffice.dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-ad-permit/) includes electronic advertisements. Ask the appointed professional to confirm the applicable permission and accurate listing details before the images are published. Requirements elsewhere need to be checked with the relevant authority.

Prepare an inventory of what is included in the sale and what is only there for presentation. Refer to the [property-photography guide](/journal/property-photography-uae) when briefing the photographer, especially if personal possessions, neighbouring homes or digitally altered images could create confusion.

sections.heading: Make the setup manageable while you still live there
sections.body:
A staging arrangement that takes an hour to rebuild before every viewing will soon become frustrating. Keep a short reset list for the rooms visitors will see: clear surfaces, return furniture to its agreed position, put private documents away and check the lighting. Share the list with anyone else living in the home.

Plan around children, pets and normal working routines. The property does not need to look unoccupied, but it should be ready for an agreed appointment without a last-minute rush. If an item is essential for daily life, find a sensible place for it instead of pretending it does not exist.

Review the arrangement after the first few viewings. If several visitors misunderstand a room's size or function, change the presentation that is causing the confusion. Keep the changes specific and affordable. The best result is a home that visitors can understand and that you can continue to live in comfortably while it is marketed.

aliyas-journal-054.excerpt: Commission photographs that make the layout, light and condition easy to understand. A useful listing gallery earns attention without changing what a buyer will find at the viewing.
aliyas-journal-054.introduction:
A beautiful photograph can earn a click. A useful set of photographs helps someone decide whether the home could suit them. Those are related jobs, but they are not quite the same. A gallery full of close-ups, dramatic windows and decorative objects may say very little about the rooms themselves.

Before commissioning a shoot, decide what the buyer needs to understand. The strongest brief connects the entrance, living spaces, bedrooms and practical areas into a believable account of the property. Presentation matters; so does leaving the photographer enough time and information to do that job properly.
takeaways: Show the property's layout and everyday spaces, not just its most decorative corners.
Agree image rights, deliverables and editing boundaries before the shoot.
Review the finished gallery against the actual home and approved listing details.

sections.heading: Write a brief that goes beyond the hero image
sections.body:
Start with the likely questions. Where is the dining area in relation to the kitchen? Does the bedroom have space around the bed? How does the balcony connect to the living room? Ask the photographer for a sequence that answers these questions, including connecting views where useful.

List important spaces that are easy to overlook: the entrance, laundry area, storage and parking arrangement. Some may need a photograph, while others are better explained in the floor plan or listing text. The aim is coverage that helps a buyer understand the home, rather than a fixed number of images regardless of its layout.

Discuss the intended uses before agreeing a fee. Portal images, a website cover and vertical social posts may need different crops. Confirm who can use the files, for how long, whether the broker can reuse them and what happens when the listing changes. Put the agreed deliverables and licence in writing.

sections.heading: Prepare the occupied home before the camera arrives
sections.body:
Clean windows and reflective surfaces, put away laundry and clear enough worktop space to show the kitchen. Keep the rooms recognisable as places people can actually use. The separate [home-staging guide](/journal/home-staging-uae) covers furniture placement and practical presentation before the shoot.

Privacy deserves its own check. Look for family photographs, certificates, computer screens, letters, medication labels and identifying information on a child's bedroom wall. Move them before photography instead of relying on extensive editing afterwards. Agree access and permission with the occupants; a marketing appointment does not settle questions about entering an occupied home.

Have one person available to answer questions about the property and move small items safely. Confirm which fittings are included in the sale so the photographs do not create the wrong impression. If a room is temporarily inaccessible or repair work is unfinished, decide how that will be explained rather than quietly leaving a significant gap in the gallery.

sections.heading: Ask for believable light and proportions
sections.body:
Watch how the rooms look at different times before choosing the appointment. Tell the photographer when direct sun makes a room difficult to photograph or when the view is obscured by glare. Access to a terrace or shared facility may also affect the schedule, so check it in advance.

[Adobe's real-estate photography guidance](https://www.adobe.com/creativecloud/photography/type/real-estate-photography.html) discusses mixed lighting and keeping the camera level to avoid distorted verticals. Those are useful technical considerations: inconsistent light colour and leaning walls can distract from the space. Leave the photographic settings to the professional, while agreeing that the result should represent the room fairly.

Review wide views carefully. A photograph should help explain a room without making a narrow passage look like a generous living area. Ask for another angle if the proportions feel implausible. Retain a normal view of the window outlook as well as any detail shot; the surroundings are part of what the buyer is assessing.

table.caption: A gallery brief organised around buyer questions
rows: How do the main activities fit together?
A clear room view and a connecting angle
An honest view of the usable space
How does the home work day to day?
Work areas, storage and relevant connections
What can the occupant actually use?
Access, proportions and the real outlook
table.note: An editorial planning framework, not a required photographic specification.

sections.heading: Build a sequence with a clear beginning
sections.body:
Choose a lead photograph that represents the property well at the small size used in search results. It might be the main living space or an exterior with a clear connection to the home. Avoid selecting a spectacular shared facility if it leaves viewers unsure which property is actually being offered.

Arrange the following images as a sensible walk through the home. Show a room before its details and keep repeated angles to a useful minimum. A photograph of a tap is rarely more helpful than a missing bedroom. If the property has several similar rooms, identify them accurately so the gallery is not mistaken for multiple views of one room.

Shared facilities need clear captions and appropriate permission. Explain that a pool or gym belongs to the building or community rather than the private unit. Recheck the sequence on a phone, where excessive repetition is especially noticeable and the first few images carry much of the explanation.

sections.heading: Set boundaries for editing and virtual staging
sections.body:
Agree what the editor may change before the files arrive. Correcting exposure or removing an accidental colour cast is different from removing a building outside the window, enlarging a balcony or hiding damage. The latter changes can materially alter what someone believes they are viewing.

If digitally furnished images are used, label them clearly and provide an unaltered view of the same room. A proposed layout should not imply that furniture is included or that an alteration has approval. Keep the original files and a record of which versions are being used in the listing.

Inspect the final images beside the property fact sheet. Check views, fixtures and captions, not just whether the pictures are attractive. If the home changes after the shoot, update the relevant images. An older gallery showing furniture or a condition that no longer exists should not remain the only visual account of the property.

sections.heading: Approve the listing as a complete package
sections.body:
Photographs work alongside the written description, floor plan and viewing arrangements. Compare them before publication so the same room count, occupancy status and included items appear throughout. Our guide to [planning property viewings](/journal/plan-property-viewings-uae) helps connect the online presentation with the visit itself.

In Dubai, [DLD's Madmoun announcement](https://dubailand.gov.ae/en/news-media/dubai-land-department-provides-madmoun-service-to-verify-validity-of-real-estate-ads-via-qr-codes) explains the QR-code service associated with real-estate advertising permits. It gives consumers a way to check authorised advertisement information. Have the responsible broker confirm the current advertising requirements; a polished photograph does not replace that process.

Keep approved files together with their captions and usage permission. Give the broker one final gallery rather than several unlabelled revisions. After publication, inspect both mobile and desktop versions for crops that cut off important features. If questions repeatedly concern a room the gallery barely shows, improve that coverage instead of adding more decorative photographs.

aliyas-journal-055.excerpt: Look past the labels when comparing agency appointments. The agreement, marketing responsibilities, reporting and exit terms determine how the selling arrangement will work.
aliyas-journal-055.introduction:
Two brokers can describe their service using the same word and still offer very different arrangements. An exclusive appointment might include a carefully managed campaign or little more than permission to advertise. An open arrangement might be coordinated effectively or produce conflicting prices and duplicate messages.

For a seller, the useful question is who will be responsible for each part of the work and what the contract actually requires. Neither label is a substitute for reading the appointment. Local advertising rules also matter, so a practice described in another emirate should not be assumed to apply to your property.
takeaways: Read the agreed scope, duration and payment triggers before choosing a listing approach.
Check the emirate's advertising framework rather than assuming unlimited broker access.
Assign clear responsibility for listing accuracy, buyer records and feedback.

sections.heading: Define the arrangement before comparing the promises
sections.body:
Ask each broker to describe the proposed appointment in plain language. Who may market the property? Can another broker introduce a buyer? What happens if someone approaches you directly? Which circumstances trigger a commission, and when does it become payable? The written agreement should answer these questions without relying on an informal understanding.

Exclusivity generally concerns limits on other appointments or marketing rights, but its precise effect depends on the contract and applicable rules. Do not assume that every exclusive agreement has the same exception for a seller's own buyer. Equally, a non-exclusive arrangement does not remove the need to agree terms with each participating broker.

Obtain clarification before signing if two clauses seem inconsistent. A short written explanation tied to the actual clause is more useful than a broad reassurance that the terms are standard. Take independent advice where the financial or legal consequences are unclear, particularly if an earlier appointment is still running.

sections.heading: Check the local advertising framework
sections.body:
In Dubai, [DLD's Form A circular](https://dubailand.gov.ae/media/io2f5x5c/%D8%B1%D8%A8%D8%B7-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%B5%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%AD-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B9%D9%82%D8%A7%D8%B1%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A8%D8%B9%D9%82%D8%AF-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%B3%D9%88%D9%8A%D9%82-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%83%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%88%D9%86%D9%8A.pdf) connects the electronic seller-broker marketing contract with advertising permits. The appointment and the permission to advertise therefore need to be considered together. Ask the broker to explain the current process for your property, including how changes to the appointment affect the listing.

Abu Dhabi has its own framework. The [ADREC Madhmoun FAQ](https://adrec.gov.ae/en/faqs) states that a property may have a maximum of three approved advertising brokers. That is an Abu Dhabi platform rule, not a reason to assume the same number applies across the UAE or that any three agencies can advertise without approval.

Before choosing a structure, identify the competent authority and the person handling the required registrations or permits. Keep a record of which agencies are authorised to advertise and which version of the property information they should use. More advertisements are not automatically evidence of a better organised sale.

sections.heading: What a well-managed exclusive appointment should clarify
sections.body:
A single lead broker can give the seller one point of contact, but that benefit depends on a clear service plan. Ask who will handle enquiries when the named broker is unavailable, how viewings will be arranged and how feedback will be reported. The agreement should be supported by practical commitments that can be checked.

Discuss the campaign rather than accepting a general promise of maximum exposure. Which channels will be used? Who pays for professional photography? How will cooperating brokers be treated? What information will you receive about enquiries and offers? An appointment that restricts your alternatives deserves a particularly clear explanation of the work being undertaken.

Agree a review date and the evidence to bring to it. Enquiry counts alone do not explain why buyers are declining. A useful report distinguishes unsuitable enquiries, completed viewings, recurring objections and offers received. Decide in advance how you will address weak execution or inaccurate advertising within the contract's terms.

table.caption: Questions to ask under either arrangement
rows: Dates, notice and any continuing obligations
table.note: Comparison framework only. The signed agreement and applicable law determine the actual rights and obligations.

sections.heading: What an open arrangement needs to work well
sections.body:
When more than one broker is involved, the seller needs a reliable way to keep information consistent. Distribute one approved description, asking price, image set and access procedure. If the price changes, update every authorised listing promptly. Contradictory advertisements can leave buyers unsure which information is current.

Keep an enquiry and introduction record through an agreed process that respects personal information. Ask the brokers how they handle a buyer who contacts more than one agency and whether any cooperation arrangement exists. Do not promise payment to one party while ignoring obligations already agreed with another.

Viewings need coordination too. Several agencies booking independently can create repeated disruption for the occupants and unnecessary confusion at reception. Set a single appointment channel or shared confirmation procedure. If managing the agencies becomes a separate job you cannot realistically undertake, account for that burden when deciding whether the arrangement suits you.

sections.heading: Compare the commercial terms on the same page
sections.body:
Put the proposed agreements side by side and record their duration, commission basis, additional charges, marketing costs and cancellation provisions. Check whether quoted amounts include applicable taxes and whether any payment is due if you withdraw, reject an offer or sell through a different introduction. Do not assume a familiar percentage explains the whole obligation.

Ask how the broker's duties continue after an offer is accepted. Negotiation, document coordination and handover support may have different scopes. The [offer-comparison guide](/journal/compare-property-offers-beyond-price) explains why the buyer's conditions and timing deserve attention alongside the price; clarify who will help you obtain that information.

Also agree ownership and permitted use of commissioned photographs. Our [property-photography guide](/journal/property-photography-uae) covers the questions to settle before paying for a shoot. If you later change brokers, knowing which files may be reused can prevent an avoidable dispute or a second photography bill.

sections.heading: Choose an arrangement you can review fairly
sections.body:
Decide what a satisfactory first review would look like before the campaign begins. That might mean accurate listings, appointments handled reliably, a useful feedback record and an explanation of the buyer response. These are observable aspects of the service, even when a sale has not yet been agreed.

A quiet first week does not by itself prove the appointment is wrong. Nor does a high volume of messages prove the strategy is working. Examine whether the property is reaching suitable buyers and whether repeated questions point to presentation, price, access or a mismatch with the likely audience.

If a change becomes necessary, check notice requirements and any continuing commission provisions before appointing someone else. Obtain written confirmation of the transition and removal or amendment of advertisements. The best arrangement for your situation is one whose responsibilities you understand and whose execution you can assess, rather than the one with the most appealing label.

references.label: DLD: electronic marketing contract and advertising permits
references.period: Circular 01-2022, 14 July 2022; checked 30 October 2026

references.label: ADREC: Madhmoun frequently asked questions
references.period: Current Abu Dhabi platform guidance checked 30 October 2026

aliyas-journal-056.excerpt: Give buyers enough time and clear information to understand the home. A thoughtful viewing plan covers access, occupants, the route through the rooms and the questions that follow.
aliyas-journal-056.introduction:
A viewing often goes wrong before anyone reaches the front door. The visitor cannot find the entrance, the building has not approved access or the occupant has been given a different appointment time. None of that helps someone assess whether the property fits their life.

A well-run visit feels straightforward because the practical work has already been done. Buyers can look, ask questions and understand the layout without being rushed through a performance. The seller, broker and occupants also know what to expect. That coordination is especially valuable when the property remains someone's home.
takeaways: Confirm access, timing and occupant arrangements before accepting an appointment.
Let the route explain the layout and leave time for practical questions.
Record specific feedback rather than treating every polite compliment as buying interest.

sections.heading: Make the appointment useful before it starts
sections.body:
Give the broker a concise access sheet covering the correct entrance, visitor parking, reception arrangements and any booking requirements for shared facilities. Check the instructions yourself. A map pin at the centre of a large development may still leave someone a long way from the actual entrance.

Ask prospective buyers what they need to understand from the visit. A household with a large dining table may want to measure the dining area; someone working from home may be interested in room separation and everyday noise. These questions help prepare the visit without requiring unnecessary personal information.

Confirm who will attend and leave a sensible gap before the next appointment. Give visitors a contact for delays and explain how to cancel. If an important space cannot be accessed, say so beforehand and arrange another way to inspect it. Surprising the buyer with a locked room makes the visit less productive.

sections.heading: Agree access with the people living there
sections.body:
Occupied viewings need cooperation. Discuss suitable windows, notice arrangements, pets, working hours and whether the occupants would prefer to remain present. Do not assume a seller's marketing plan overrides the lease or gives unrestricted entry. The actual tenancy and applicable local requirements need to be respected.

Dubai's [Law No. 26 of 2007, Article 28](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2007/Law%20No.%20%2826%29%20of%202007.html) protects a tenant's right to occupy under a fixed-term lease when ownership changes. A sale and a vacant handover are therefore different questions. The [tenanted-property selling guide](/journal/selling-tenanted-property-uae) addresses that distinction and the need for property-specific advice.

Agree rules for opening cupboards, taking photographs and accessing private areas. Put sensitive paperwork and valuables away before the appointment. If circumstances change, reconfirm the visit rather than relying on an old message. A reliable routine is easier for occupants to accommodate than a succession of last-minute demands.

sections.heading: Choose a route that explains how the home works
sections.body:
Begin with a short orientation at the entrance. Point out the relationship between the main living area, kitchen and bedrooms, then let the buyer see those connections in person. A good route follows the layout rather than jumping between whichever rooms look most impressive.

Leave space for the visitor to stand back and look. Explain practical features such as storage, laundry access and where larger furniture could fit, without claiming a particular item will fit unless it has been measured. Show relevant shared spaces when access is permitted, making their relationship to the private home clear.

Keep the home comfortable and the presentation believable. Strong fragrance, loud music or an excessive number of decorative objects can distract from the property. The [staging guide](/journal/home-staging-uae) offers preparation ideas that help buyers understand the space without disguising its condition.

table.caption: A viewing route built around practical questions
table.note: Adapt the route to the property and agreed access. This is not a required order or a fixed appointment duration.

sections.heading: Answer accurately, including when the answer is not ready
sections.body:
Prepare a short factual pack with the documented area, included fittings, occupancy position and information the owner is authorised to share. Keep it consistent with the listing. If a service cost, alteration approval or maintenance question is unresolved, record it as unresolved rather than estimating confidently during the visit.

Distinguish what you have observed from what needs a professional assessment. A room feeling quiet during a short appointment does not establish its sound-insulation performance. A recently painted ceiling does not explain the history of a leak. Buyers should be able to ask follow-up questions and arrange appropriate checks through the agreed process.

Avoid turning every question into a sales response. Someone asking about afternoon sun needs information about the room, not a general statement that the home is bright and luxurious. A clear answer, or a commitment to obtain the right document, helps the buyer make a more informed decision.

sections.heading: Treat an open house as a separate operational choice
sections.body:
Several appointments grouped together may reduce repeated preparation, but an open house also needs a plan for reception, access, privacy and the number of people inside. Consider whether the occupants and building can accommodate it. More visitors at once can make detailed questions harder to handle.

[DLD's real-estate advertisement permit service](https://backoffice.dubailand.gov.ae/en/eservices/real-estate-ad-permit/) includes open-house events among its listed permit types. For a Dubai property, have the responsible broker confirm the applicable permission and arrangements before promoting an event. Do not treat an ordinary viewing appointment and a publicly advertised event as automatically interchangeable.

Agree who supervises each area and how attendees are recorded with appropriate privacy care. Keep keys and documents controlled. If the home is small or access is restricted, individual appointments may provide a clearer experience. Choose the format for the property and people involved, not simply because an event sounds more ambitious.

sections.heading: Turn the follow-up into useful information
sections.body:
After the visit, ask what the buyer understood well and what remains unclear. Record specific objections in their own context: a bedroom may be too small for that household, or a move-in date may not match their plans. Those are different issues from an inaccurate floor plan or unanswered maintenance question.

Look for patterns across several visits without overreacting to one preference. If buyers repeatedly cannot understand the dining layout, improve the photographs or plan. If the same cost question keeps arising, obtain the relevant evidence. A useful feedback record separates presentation problems from features the seller cannot change.

Finally, close the loop on promised answers. Send the requested information through the broker and keep a record of what was provided. Do not pressure someone to make an offer before an important question is resolved. A well-organised viewing ends with a clear next step, whether that is a second visit, further checks or an honest decision that the home is unsuitable.

aliyas-journal-057.excerpt: A tenanted home can be sold, but ownership transfer and vacant possession are separate matters. Begin with the lease, communicate carefully and make the proposed handover position explicit.
aliyas-journal-057.introduction:
For the owner, the property may be an asset being sold. For the tenant, it remains home. A workable sale plan has to recognise both realities, alongside the buyer's intended use. An investor willing to take over an occupied property may ask different questions from a household hoping to move in soon.

The first task is therefore to establish what can actually be offered. Do not advertise a vacant handover date merely because that date would suit the sale. This guide uses Dubai law for specific legal examples; other emirates require their own tenancy and transaction checks.
takeaways: Keep ownership transfer, lease expiry and lawful possession as separate questions.
Check the actual tenancy file and obtain advice before making notice or vacancy promises.
Agree how rent, deposits, records and occupant communication will be handled at transfer.

sections.heading: Establish the tenancy position before writing the listing
sections.body:
Collect the signed lease and renewals, registration record where applicable, payment schedule, deposit record, agreed amendments and relevant correspondence. Check who is named as landlord and tenant, which property is covered and whether any separate parking or storage agreement exists. A summary from memory is not enough to brief a buyer accurately.

Record the current contractual dates and any unresolved dispute or maintenance issue. If a notice has been issued, preserve the actual document and evidence of service for professional review. Do not reduce a complicated position to a line saying that the tenant will leave soon.

Decide what information can appropriately be shared at each stage. A buyer needs an accurate account of the tenancy, but that does not justify circulating identity documents or private tenant correspondence with a public listing. Use controlled disclosure through the transaction process, with sensitive material limited to the people who need it.

sections.heading: Separate the sale from the right to vacant possession
sections.body:
Under [Dubai Law No. 26 of 2007, Article 28](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2007/Law%20No.%20%2826%29%20of%202007.html), transferring ownership does not remove the tenant's right to occupy under a fixed-term lease. A buyer should not assume that becoming the owner ends the existing tenancy. Check the contract and the applicable legal position before agreeing a move-in timetable.

[Law No. 33 of 2008's amended Article 25](https://dlp.dubai.gov.ae/Legislation%20Reference/2009/Law%20No.%20%2833%29%20of%202008%20Amending%20Law%20No.%20%2826%29%20of%202007.pdf) includes an owner's wish to sell among the grounds for seeking eviction on lease expiry. It requires at least twelve months' notice of the eviction reason, served through a notary public or registered mail. This is a Dubai provision, not a UAE-wide notice rule.

Those provisions are not a substitute for advice on a particular case. Whether a notice is valid, how it interacts with the lease and what happens following a sale can involve issues beyond this overview. Have a qualified adviser review the documents and current requirements. Do not infer a guaranteed possession date from the existence of a notice alone.

sections.heading: Describe the offer in terms a buyer can assess
sections.body:
Be explicit about whether the property is being offered subject to the current tenancy or with a proposed vacant handover that still needs conditions to be satisfied. State the distinction consistently in the listing, viewing discussions and proposed agreement. Unclear marketing can attract buyers whose plans cannot be accommodated.

An investor may want to understand rent receipts, arrears, recurring costs and the remaining lease term. An intended owner-occupier will be especially concerned with lawful availability and the consequences if their desired date is not achievable. Neither should be asked to rely on an informal assurance that the tenant is cooperative.

Prepare a question log and obtain answers before negotiations become urgent. The [offer-comparison guide](/journal/compare-property-offers-beyond-price) helps distinguish price from conditions and timing. A seemingly attractive offer can become impractical if it depends on a possession promise the seller cannot support.

table.caption: Clarify these points before agreeing the handover position
rows: What money is held or due?
table.note: Planning questions, not legal conclusions about a particular lease, notice or dispute.

sections.heading: Make viewings manageable for the tenant
sections.body:
Introduce the marketing plan calmly and identify one contact for access arrangements. Agree practical appointment windows, how requests will be confirmed and what happens if a visit has to be moved. Do not let several brokers make independent arrangements that repeatedly disrupt the household.

Discuss photography separately from viewings. Personal belongings, documents and family photographs may need to be moved or excluded from images. Agree which areas can be photographed and how the property will be presented without implying that the tenant's furniture forms part of the sale.

Keep visits focused and respect the agreed boundaries. The [property-viewing guide](/journal/plan-property-viewings-uae) covers the operational details. This cooperation is valuable, but it does not replace the tenancy contract or legal requirements. If access is disputed, seek appropriate advice rather than escalating through unannounced visits or pressure on the occupant.

sections.heading: Reconcile the financial and management handover
sections.body:
Before completion, ask the professionals handling the sale to prepare a clear settlement record. Identify rent already received, amounts still outstanding, the deposit held and any agreed allocation between seller and buyer. The treatment should reflect the actual documents and agreement, not a calculation improvised at the transfer appointment.

Keep maintenance responsibilities and open issues visible. A pending repair, warranty claim or contractor appointment may need to pass to the new owner or manager. Record the status, relevant contact and any agreed responsibility so the tenant is not left repeating the history to several people.

Confirm how the tenant will be notified of the ownership change and any verified payment or management instructions. Avoid sending conflicting account details through informal channels. The buyer, seller and advisers should agree the required steps and documents, while protecting the tenant from uncertainty about who is authorised to receive payments or arrange work.

sections.heading: Keep the final agreement aligned with the evidence
sections.body:
Review every possession statement in the proposed sale terms. If the property remains occupied, the contract and handover record should reflect that position. If vacant possession is a condition, obtain advice on the wording, responsibilities and consequences if it cannot lawfully be achieved on time.

Do not rely on a promise made during a viewing to resolve an issue that should be documented. Ask for the parties' agreed position on keys, access devices, tenancy records and any outstanding matters. Where a tenant has separately agreed to move, have the arrangement reviewed and properly recorded rather than assuming a verbal understanding is sufficient.

A smooth sale is not necessarily the quickest possible departure of the occupant. It is a transfer whose legal, financial and practical position is understood. That gives the seller a clearer commitment to make, the buyer a more realistic basis for planning and the tenant a more orderly experience.

references.period: Original tenancy law, read with amendments; checked 30 October 2026

references.label: Dubai Law No. 33 of 2008 amending the tenancy law

aliyas-journal-058.excerpt: Compare what each buyer is offering in full: price, conditions, funding, costs and completion arrangements. The largest headline amount is only the beginning of the decision.
aliyas-journal-058.introduction:
One buyer offers more but needs a longer timetable and several conditions. Another offers slightly less with a different funding position. Which offer is better? There is no useful answer until the details are put on the same basis.

Sellers can become anchored to a headline figure because it is easy to compare. The less visible terms may determine whether the proposed sale can complete and how much money is available afterwards. A disciplined comparison makes those terms visible without pretending that any offer is risk-free or that a simple score can replace judgement.
takeaways: Obtain the full written terms before treating two offers as comparable.
Separate the sale price, estimated net proceeds and certainty of completion.
Use evidence for funding and conditions; do not turn assumptions into guarantees.

sections.heading: Begin with a complete offer record
sections.body:
Record the offered price, buyer identity through the appropriate process, proposed dates, deposit arrangements, inclusions and every condition. Note whether the buyer needs finance, a valuation, the sale of another property or further inspections. Ask when outstanding matters are expected to be resolved and who will confirm them.

Avoid filling gaps with optimistic assumptions. An offer described as cash still needs appropriate verification and a workable payment process. A financed offer needs more detail than a statement that the buyer has spoken to a bank. The broker and relevant professionals should help establish what evidence is appropriate without distributing sensitive documents unnecessarily.

Keep each offer version dated. If a buyer changes the price, timing or inclusions, update the whole record rather than comparing the newest amount against old conditions. A clear paper trail also helps prevent a verbal concession from being remembered differently when the agreement is prepared.

sections.heading: Separate funding evidence from confidence
sections.body:
Ask what has actually been completed in the buyer's financing process and what remains conditional. A preliminary indication, a property valuation and final approval are different stages. Have the responsible lender or adviser explain the outstanding requirements rather than assuming one document resolves every financing question.

Your own mortgage matters too. [HSBC UAE's mortgage-management guidance](https://www.hsbc.ae/mortgages/manage-your-mortgage/) explains that a mortgaged sale involves settlement and release arrangements, with processes that differ according to the buyer's funding. Use the instructions from your actual lender; another bank's process is not a promise about your transaction.

[Emirates NBD's liability-letter guidance](https://www.emiratesnbd.com/en/help-and-support/request-a-liability-or-no-liability-letter) describes a letter confirming financial obligations. Ask your lender which settlement document is needed, what it covers and how long the figures remain usable. An old balance from a banking app is not a substitute for a current settlement instruction. Resolve these dependencies before treating an ambitious completion date as certain.

sections.heading: Compare estimated net proceeds on consistent assumptions
sections.body:
Create a separate calculation for each offer using the same categories. Begin with the sale price, deduct the seller's applicable transaction costs and agreed concessions, then account for any lender settlement. Identify estimates clearly and obtain current figures before committing. Taxes, if relevant to the owner's circumstances, need appropriate separate advice.

The example below is deliberately invented. Offer A is AED 2,000,000 with an assumed AED 60,000 seller cost allowance. Offer B is AED 1,980,000 with an assumed AED 30,000 allowance. Both assume AED 900,000 lender settlement. The resulting amounts are AED 1,040,000 and AED 1,050,000 respectively, before any other applicable adjustments.

This does not establish that a lower offer is better. The cost allowances are not UAE fee schedules, and the example says nothing about either buyer's reliability. It demonstrates why price and proceeds are separate calculations. Replace every assumption with the actual proposed allocation and current evidence.

table.caption: Illustrative comparison: price is not the same as proceeds
table.note: Invented scenario. Remainder = price minus assumed costs minus settlement; before other applicable adjustments. Not market quotes or a recommendation.

chart.title: Illustrative cash remaining under two offers
chart.note: Invented inputs shown in the table. Not actual offers, standard fees, guaranteed proceeds or evidence of completion certainty.

sections.heading: Read the conditions as a sequence of decisions
sections.body:
List the conditions in the order they must be resolved. For each one, identify the responsible party, required evidence and proposed deadline. Ask the professional preparing the agreement to explain what happens if it is not satisfied. Do not assume that a condition is harmless because it appears in familiar wording.

Some conditions may be essential and reasonable, such as a buyer needing to complete appropriate checks. The issue is whether the parties understand their effect. A deadline that depends on several unfinished steps needs more scrutiny than a date selected because it looks convenient on a calendar.

Compare any request for vacant possession, repairs or included furniture separately from price. If the home is tenanted, make sure the proposed condition reflects the actual tenancy position. A concession that seems small during negotiation can become a serious obligation when the seller cannot deliver it as promised.

sections.heading: Consider time without inventing a probability of success
sections.body:
Work out what a later completion means for your own costs and plans. There may be additional accommodation, finance, storage or moving expenses, but use actual quotations and terms where available. Do not convert inconvenience into an arbitrary discount and present it as a precise financial result.

Also consider what happens if the proposed sale does not complete. Are you delaying another purchase, turning away other enquiries or arranging a move? Ask for advice on the agreement's remedies and commitments. A larger deposit or shorter timetable is not, by itself, proof that every risk has been removed.

Avoid assigning invented percentages to the chance of completion. A useful comparison can say that a particular approval is outstanding or that funds have been evidenced through the appropriate process. Those statements are clearer and more defensible than calling one buyer ninety per cent certain without a basis for that number.

sections.heading: Negotiate the package and record the result
sections.body:
Identify the few terms that matter most to you. One seller may need flexibility around moving; another may need certainty about included fixtures or the allocation of a cost. Discuss those needs alongside the price rather than repeatedly countering with a number while leaving the practical conflict unresolved.

Use the [asking-price guide](/journal/asking-price-dubai-home) to keep price discussions connected to evidence about the property. Then use the [listing-to-handover guide](/journal/uae-home-seller-planning-guide) to check whether the proposed timetable can be supported by the necessary documents and arrangements.

Before accepting, review the final written offer as a whole. Confirm that concessions made in separate conversations have been captured accurately and that superseded versions cannot cause confusion. The aim is a decision you can explain: what you expect to receive, what you must deliver and which uncertainties remain. That is a stronger basis for a sale than choosing solely by the largest headline amount.

aliyas-journal-059.excerpt: Organise the sale as a sequence of dependent steps, from the listing file to the final handover record. Clear responsibilities matter more than an optimistic completion date.
aliyas-journal-059.introduction:
Accepting an offer can feel like the finish line. In practice, it begins a different phase of the sale: turning agreed terms into a transfer that the parties, lender, developer and relevant authority can complete. Missing documents or unclear responsibilities are easier to resolve before everyone has arranged their moving dates.

There is no single timetable that fits every UAE home. A cash sale of an unencumbered property differs from a mortgaged sale, an occupied home or an off-plan assignment. This planning guide concerns an existing home and helps you organise the questions for the professionals handling the transaction.
takeaways: Assign a responsible person and evidence requirement to each stage.
Use the current developer, lender and authority instructions for the actual property.
Keep transfer, possession, utility arrangements and the physical handover record distinct.

sections.heading: Build the sale file before the campaign starts
sections.body:
Keep ownership documents, the property fact sheet, relevant plans, alteration records and any tenancy information in a controlled folder. Identify which items are complete, which need updating and who will obtain the missing records. Names and property identifiers should be checked across the file before they are copied into agreements.

Agree the broker's appointment, advertising arrangements, asking price and access procedure. Our [sale-preparation guide](/journal/prepare-uae-property-for-sale) covers the condition and presentation work that sits alongside this file. Good preparation reduces the number of basic questions arriving at the same time as an offer deadline.

If an owner is overseas, a company owns the home or someone will sign under a power of attorney, raise that immediately with the relevant professionals. Do not assume a document accepted for another purpose will be sufficient for this transaction. The authority and those handling the sale need to confirm the current requirements.

sections.heading: Turn the accepted offer into a workable agreement
sections.body:
Review the price together with the conditions, payment arrangements, proposed dates and possession position. Make sure the agreed inclusions are clear. Furniture, access devices, appliances and outstanding repairs should not depend on what either party remembers from a viewing conversation.

The [offer-comparison guide](/journal/compare-property-offers-beyond-price) explains how to assess those terms before acceptance. Once the parties are ready to proceed, ask the professional preparing the agreement to explain deadlines, responsibilities and the consequences of an unmet condition. Sign only when the actual obligations are understood.

Create a shared transaction checklist from the agreed terms. It should identify the next action, responsible person and required evidence without exposing sensitive documents to everyone. Update the checklist when a dependency changes. A completion date is useful as a target, but it should not conceal unfinished steps that make the date unrealistic.

sections.heading: Confirm the developer and lender dependencies
sections.body:
For a relevant property, obtain the developer's current resale requirements directly. The [Dubai Properties guide for handed-over homes with title deeds](https://dp.ae/pdf/DP_Resale%20Guide_Handed%20Over%202025.pdf) describes its resale NOC process and states that the issued NOC is valid for thirty days. That is a developer-specific example: it should not be treated as the validity period for every UAE development.

If a mortgage is involved, ask the actual lender for its settlement and release instructions. [HSBC UAE's guidance](https://www.hsbc.ae/mortgages/manage-your-mortgage/) illustrates how the process changes with the buyer's funding route. Coordinate these instructions with the proposed transfer rather than assuming a statement of the outstanding loan is enough.

Record expiry dates and prerequisites in the checklist. Ask what must be refreshed if the transfer is delayed, including figures or approvals that are only valid for a limited period. Avoid requesting time-limited documents so early that they expire while another necessary stage remains unresolved.

table.caption: A transaction checklist with clear ownership
table.note: Adapt this planning sequence to the transaction. It does not replace an authority's or lender's procedure.

sections.heading: Prepare the transfer without relying on informal instructions
sections.body:
Confirm the competent registration authority and authorised transfer channel for the property. Obtain the current document and payment requirements from the people handling that process. Check the identities and authority of anyone who will sign or receive funds through the appropriate professional channels.

Reconfirm payment instructions securely, especially if details change close to completion. Do not act solely on an unexpected message containing a new account. Keep the agreed settlement statement and supporting calculations available so that costs, lender amounts and any adjustments can be reviewed before the appointment.

Make practical arrangements for attendance, representation and original documents where required. A buyer's travel booking or a seller's removal van does not override a missing approval. If a dependency is unresolved, communicate that promptly and obtain advice on the contractual implications rather than hoping the issue can be repaired at the transfer desk.

sections.heading: Coordinate services and possession carefully
sections.body:
Utilities, building access and physical possession need their own plan. Identify whose account serves the property and whether it will be closed, transferred or remain associated with an existing tenant. Do not disconnect an occupied tenant's services simply because ownership is changing.

[DEWA's clearance-certificate guidance](https://dewa.gov.ae/en/about-us/service-guide/consumer-services/request-for-clearance-certificate) explains the relationship between clearance and outstanding amounts in its Dubai service process. Confirm the appropriate request for the actual account and sale situation. A clearance document, an account closure and the moment the buyer receives possession are separate operational matters; they should not be assumed to happen automatically together.

Agree meter records where relevant, access-card arrangements and how building management will be informed. Keep instructions consistent across the parties. If the home remains tenanted, coordinate the tenancy and management records instead of preparing a vacant-home handover that does not match the sale terms.

sections.heading: Finish with a useful handover record
sections.body:
Walk through the property against the agreed condition and inclusions. Record keys, cards, remotes, manuals and any items that remain outstanding. If photographs are appropriate, use them to document the actual condition at handover, with the parties' agreement, rather than relying on the older marketing gallery.

Explain practical information the new owner needs, such as the location of relevant controls and available warranty documents. Do not offer technical assurances beyond the evidence you hold. An unresolved repair or missing access device should be recorded with the agreed next action instead of disappearing into a verbal promise.

Keep the final sale, settlement and handover records securely after completion. Remove obsolete advertisements through the responsible broker and update any remaining management contacts. A transaction is easier to close cleanly when the last stage has the same care as the launch: accurate records, named responsibilities and a clear account of what has actually been delivered.
